subject: The secret warning relationship experts won't tell you
preview_text: What therapists and reviewers are quietly saying about scanning conversations. This changes everything.
body_paragraphs: I got an email last week from a licensed couples therapist. She said something that stopped me cold. She told me she's started quietly recommending my app to clients who can't see what's right in front of them. Not as a replacement for therapy, but as a 'reality check tool.'

The Atlantic just published a piece on 'digital relationship audits.' Forbes called this approach 'the unspoken hack for modern dating.' The consensus? The most dangerous red flags are the ones we normalize. Experts say we're wired to explain away toxicity, to make excuses for the gut feeling screaming at us. Reviewers keep mentioning one thing: the pattern detection. Seeing the same manipulative language pop up across weeks of texts is the wake-up call nothing else provides.

That's why the dashboard inside Red Flag Scanner is built the way it is. It's not about one screenshot. It's about connecting the dots you're too close to see. The 'Relationship Health' tab shows you the trajectory. Is the love-bombing fading into criticism? Is the gaslighting becoming more frequent? The pattern map reveals what isolated moments hide.

Open the app. Go to your dashboard. Upload just two conversations from different weeks. Let the AI map the pattern. It takes 90 seconds to see what the experts are talking about. P.S. That therapist? She said the users who avoid the dashboard are the ones who need it most. Don't be that user.
